rv.q: If you leave Black Ensemble Theater’s “A Taste of Soul” without humming the chorus, “Celebrate good times, come on,” all the way home, you might be immune to the joy of live music.

The world premiere production is a knockout on every level and is sure to attract a vast New York audience hooked on the irresistible music whose “golden age” was in the 1950s, ‘60s and ‘70s — yet remains every bit as golden all these decades later.
This spectacular, smooth and sweet-sounding satire of every TV cooking show simply sizzles.
It proved to be an extraordinary event that exceeded all my expectations.
The Taste of Soul is an exuberant celebration you don't want to miss.
This is a presentation that captures the mood and texture of traditional African American food and music in a way that’s fun, exciting, and full of gusto.
The music was hot, without being imitative, the dancing was fun and adaptive of the popular presentation and hoofing of the time in question.
